nodes.title: the Qenshen signature
nodes.statement: The Qenshen system concerns objects called wrenclos. There are exactly 4 of them: glimfex, bratu, vorkeld, falzam. One operation is written #. One relation is written <~, read as "covers".

nodes.title: the Qenshen combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x # y for every pair of wrenclos is fixed by the table of the first operation. The pairs standing in the <~ relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all wrenclos x and y, x # y is again a wrenclo.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all wrenclos x, y, z: (x # y) # z = x # (y # z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all wrenclos x and y: x # y = y # x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a wrenclo glimfex with glimfex # x = x # glimfex = x for every x.

nodes.title: reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: For every wrenclo x there is a wrenclo y with x # y = y # x = glimfex.

nodes.title: cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: For all wrenclos x, y, z: if x # y = x # z then y = z.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all wrenclos x and y: if x <~ y and y <~ x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all wrenclos x, y, z: if x <~ y and y <~ z then x <~ z.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every wrenclo x: x # x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = bratu, value = glimfex, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is no wrenclo z with z # x = x # z = z for every wrenclo x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case reason = no absorbing element, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every wrenclo x: x <~ x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = bratu, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all wrenclos x and y, at least one of x <~ y and y <~ x holds.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = bratu, y = bratu, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all wrenclos x, y, z: if x <~ y then (z # x) <~ (z # y) and (x # z) <~ (y # z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = glimfex, y = glimfex, z = bratu, side = left, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: opalhurn wrenclos
nodes.statement: A wrenclo x is called opalhurn when x # x = x.

nodes.title: wrenclos that morntez
nodes.statement: Two wrenclos x and y are said to morntez when x # y = y # x.

nodes.title: mornvint collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of wrenclos is mornvint when x # y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the reldxil of a wrenclo
nodes.statement: The reldxil of a wrenclo x is the collection of wrenclos y for which x <~ y holds.

nodes.title: the ponjen
nodes.statement: The wrenclo glimfex is called the ponjen of the system. It is the unique wrenclo that leaves every wrenclo unchanged under #.

nodes.title: the tunak
nodes.statement: The tunak of the system is the collection of wrenclos that morntez with every wrenclo.

nodes.title: the shenhob
nodes.statement: The shenhob is the collection of all opalhurn wrenclos.

nodes.title: the tuclo of a wrenclo
nodes.statement: The tuclo of a wrenclo x, written [x], is the smallest mornvint collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a falkeld
nodes.statement: A wrenclo f is a falkeld when f <~ y holds for every wrenclo y, that is, when the reldxil of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: vintdri wrenclos
nodes.statement: A wrenclo x is vintdri when x # x equals the ponjen.

nodes.title: the thramorn of a wrenclo
nodes.statement: A thramorn of a wrenclo x is a wrenclo y with x # y = y # x = glimfex.

nodes.title: the iskkorr of a wrenclo
nodes.statement: The iskkorr of a wrenclo x is the number of wrenclos in its tuclo [x].

nodes.title: the wrennak
nodes.statement: The wrennak of the system is the collection of wrenclos whose iskkorr is largest.

nodes.title: grixreld pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct wrenclos x and y form a grixreld pair when x <~ y and y <~ x both hold, that is, when each lies in the reldxil of the other.

nodes.title: the ponjen is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one wrenclo e with e # x = x # e = x for every wrenclo x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every wrenclo unchanged.
Then e # f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e # f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the ponjen lies in the tunak
nodes.statement: The ponjen morntezs with every wrenclo.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the ponjen and x any wrenclo.
Then e # x = x and x # e = x.
So e # x = x # e, which is what it means to morntez.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the tunak.

nodes.title: a wrenclo has only one thramorn
nodes.statement: For every wrenclo x there is exactly one thramorn of x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y and z both be partners of x.
Then y = y # (x # z) = (y # x) # z.
Both bracketed products collapse to the neutral object.
So y = z.

nodes.title: a vintdri wrenclo is its own thramorn
nodes.statement: If x # x is the ponjen then the thramorn of x is x itself.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x be vintdri, so x # x is the ponjen.
That is exactly the condition for x to be a partner of x.
Partners are unique, so no other object can be one.

nodes.title: the tunak is mornvint
nodes.statement: If x and y both morntez with every wrenclo, then so does x # y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the tunak and let z be any wrenclo.
Then (x # y) # z = x # (y # z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each morntezs with everything.
So x # y morntezs with z, and the tunak is mornvint.

nodes.title: the tuclo of a wrenclo is mornvint
nodes.statement: For every wrenclo x, the collection [x] is mornvint.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under #.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the tuclo is contained in every mornvint collection
nodes.statement: If S is mornvint and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a wrenclo is opalhurn exactly when its iskkorr is one
nodes.statement: x # x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x # x = x then {x} is already closed under #.
So [x] = {x} and the iskkorr is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x # x, which is then x.

nodes.title: the iskkorr divides the number of wrenclos
nodes.statement: For every wrenclo x, the iskkorr of x divides 4.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is a mornvint collection.
Its size is the iskkorr of x.
The claim is that this size always divides 4.

nodes.title: the tuclo of a tunak wrenclo stays in the tunak
nodes.statement: If x lies in the tunak then every wrenclo of [x] lies in the tunak.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The tunak is mornvint.
[x] is the smallest mornvint collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the tunak is one.

nodes.title: the shenhob is mornvint
nodes.statement: If x and y are both opalhurn then so is x # y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be opalhurn.
The claim asks whether (x # y) # (x # y) returns x # y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: combining on the left never merges two wrenclos
nodes.statement: For every wrenclo a, the assignment x to a # x sends distinct wrenclos to distinct wrenclos.

verification.domain: every object translated by every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose a # x = a # y.
Cancellation on the left gives x = y.
So the assignment is injective, and being injective on a finite carrier it is onto.

nodes.title: reldxils are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the reldxil of x, then the reldxil of y is contained in the reldxil of x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x <~ y and let z satisfy y <~ z.
Transitivity gives x <~ z.
So every member of the reldxil of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one falkeld
nodes.statement: No two distinct wrenclos can both be falkelds.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f <~ h, since h is any object, and h <~ f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: no grixreld pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct wrenclos lie in each other's reldxil.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.

nodes.title: every wrenclo lies in the tunak
nodes.statement: Every pair of wrenclos morntezs.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The tunak is defined by morntezing with everything.
The claim is that x # y = y # x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every wrenclo is opalhurn breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x # x = x for every wrenclo x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = bratu, value = glimfex, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where some wrenclo reaches every other breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: There is a wrenclo whose tuclo is the whole system.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the relation reads the same in both directions breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: If x <~ y then y <~ x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = glimfex, y = bratu, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the ponjen swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e # x equals the ponjen for every wrenclo x.

verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.
